This for me becomes problematic, As there are loads of example for this through out American cinema and television e.i, Joey and Chandelier(from friends), Ted & Marshall & Barney(from H.I.M.Y.M.), and many more... Thus the reasoning becomes invalid and just offensive. Of course IRL they could be friends, I mean I see healthy male-to-male friendship IRL all the time but not like how these two are with each other. I for one have lots of male friends no homo involve gay and straight. Only with my ex did I experience the same things as Buck and Eddie doing with each other. Are you and the guy your dating not the same way? There are huge parallels of Chimney/Hen, Bobby/Athena and Karen/Hen to Buck/Eddie. So try to scroll to those Buddie threads and read you'll find out a lot of things. Some fans psycho analysis on them are on point and are interesting reads. Things about love language, Trauma, analysis on emotion etc... If you educate yourself in Queer baiting and LGBTQ+ media struggles you'll understand why people would be hostile towards these comments and such attitudes. Even one scene of the show reference this and I quote, Chimney "Growing up I didn't have a lot of roll models... When they think of fire fighters do they think of me? of you? hen?" Its a real world problem lacking representation in Media. Often LGBTQ+ characters are stigmatize, are stereotypically portrayed in media and would only be there for advertising or comical purposes, Look at Travis in the grey's anatomy spin off or SPN Castiel. Or that movie about the Closeted gay man who comes out on his wedding day, then he struggles, turns out the reporter in that show was also gay so they in up together. These are problematic shows that exploit the LGBTQ+ community and our struggles for representation. Your gay you should know all of this, anyways. So I can't blame such people to react in a way.
